title: Riyadh airport resumes flights following Houthi attacks
gist: Riyadh's King Khalid airport resumed flights after a two-week closure from Houthi strikes, but the Houthis declared it a military target; a truce collapse this summer has widened the Yemen conflict to Saudi infrastructure.

insights.claim: Riyadh's international airport said flights would resume Sunday after a two-week closure caused by Houthi strikes on the Saudi capital.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Aviation disruption in the Saudi capital is a tangible indicator of regional travel and business risk.

insights.claim: A Houthi attack this month on the Riyadh airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Casualty scale marks a step-change in Saudi domestic vulnerability.
insights.locator: Houthis have carried out waves of strikes

insights.claim: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned airlines and travellers that King Khalid Airport remains 'unsafe' and a 'military target', and said the Saudi regime would bear the consequences of any operations there.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Resumption may be followed by renewed strikes; keep airline and travel exposure to Riyadh on watch.
insights.quote: The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional, and local airlines

insights.claim: A years-long truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis broke down in the summer, and the fighting has shifted focus from the wider US-Iran war while deepening Yemen's humanitarian disaster.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Yemen is now a second front in the US-Iran confrontation, with spillover to Gulf assets.

insights.claim: The Saudi-led coalition said it shot down two drones in the Riyadh area early Sunday, the day flights resumed.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Active air defense implies continued threat tempo.
